em_ashclung.name: ash-clung
em_ashclung.hint: the Choir's anger is still on you

em_choir_approach.name: The Ash Ridge Path
em_choir_approach.desc: A switchback path climbs through drifted ash toward a ridge that glitters wrong, frost that never melts. The singing is under your feet before it's in your ears, felt through the soles more than heard. Below, the path only goes down.
onEnterOnce: This is the sound Glasswick doesn't talk about at the glassworks: layered voices, unhurried, more felt than heard, coming down off the ridge with the wind.

actions.label: read whose steps turn back here
fx: Two sets of prints climb through the ash; only one set climbs back down. Glasswick has a name for everyone who has tried this path and not finished it, and says none of them aloud.

em_choir_nave.name: The Roofless Chapel
em_choir_nave.desc: Four walls, no roof, black glass fused thick across every sill where heat once ran molten. The congregation is here still, more felt than seen in the glass's shimmer, singing low and unhurried. Ash lies banded on the floor, layer under layer under layer.
em_choir_nave.brief: Roofless walls, black glass, the Choir singing.
onEnterOnce: Count the ash bands in the broken sill and you count the fires: three, maybe four, going back further than any mason's mark left standing. Each one left the singing louder than it found it.
Brother Osk: "This is us. The Church did this — not let it happen, did it. I have never said that thought aloud before now."
Tamsin: "Four fires and it's still standing, still singing. That's not a fire that failed once. That's a fire that doesn't work here at all."
onEnter: The singing bends into words, once, plain: strike the true date from the cornerstone, let the plaque stand alone — an accident, not a decision — and we can stop being what the town still argues over.

variants.desc: Four walls and no roof, black glass fused thick across every sill. The glass has gone dull and ordinary, and nothing sings under it any longer. Ash still bands the floor, a record now, not a wound.
Four walls and no roof, black glass fused thick across every sill. The singing has thinned to something almost gentle — not gone, but no longer grieving at the top of its voice.
A fifth band of ash lies fresh over the old four, still warm underfoot. The singing did not stop. It came back inside a day, and it is louder now than the town has ever heard it.
variants.brief: A fresh fifth burning. Louder now.

actions.label: refuse the Choir, plainly
fx: You give it Brenna's buried verse instead of what it asked for, and refuse besides. It takes the verse harder than the refusal, ash needling briefly — then, first time in four hundred years, goes quiet.

You tell it no, plainly: the true date stands, never yours to give away. The ash follows you down the ridge, biting at your lungs — but under the anger, first time in four hundred years, it goes quiet.
Brother Osk: "That's it. That's the whole of it. No fire, no bargain. Just no."

actions.label: speak the Great Rite over the Choir
fx: You speak the Rite whole, needing no true date and no bargain struck. The ash-choir does not argue with it. Four hundred years of singing goes quiet at last.

actions.label: chip the date off the stone (grace)
fx: You work the true date off the cornerstone until only smooth stone answers back. Something presses the vestry's bell into your hands, whole and glad. The singing eases at once, grateful in a way that sits wrong.
Brother Osk: "It finally spoke its truth, first time in four hundred years. I keep wondering if it needed the bell too."
The chisel skips off old stone; the date's still there, still legible. It can be tried again.

actions.label: cut only the true date (wits)
fx: You read the stone once, sure which mark is the lie's only witness, and cut just that. Something presses the vestry's bell into your hands, whole and glad. The singing eases at once, grateful in a way that sits wrong.
Brother Osk: "It finally spoke its truth, first time in four hundred years. I keep wondering if it needed the bell too."
You start cutting before you're sure which line is the lie. You stop yourself in time — the date's untouched. It can be tried again.

actions.label: burn it with cinder-oil (1hp on fail)
fx: Cinder-oil spreads black over glass, the cask empty and left in the ash. The fifth fire burns fast and hot, same as the four before. By the time you're back down the path, the singing's started again, louder.
The oil catches wrong against the glass, flaring back at you before it spreads. You're driven back a step, singed, no closer to finishing what four fires before you already failed to finish.

actions.label: weigh what this grief asks
fx: The Choir has named its price: the true date struck out, the plaque left standing alone. Refuse it here and it rests, though refusing costs something real. Give it what it asks and it quiets — bargained, not rested.
The cornerstone in the fused vestry holds the one true record left of this. Read it — the Choir will not speak plainly to you until you have.
The burn stands ready: a cask of cinder-oil is yours (might; a failed try costs 1 hp).
The burn wants cinder-oil — Factor Corrin will give it, bound by doctrine, at the Ironbound Scale-House.

em_choir_vestry.name: The Fused Vestry
em_choir_vestry.desc: A side room, roof half-collapsed, its robing-chest and shelves run together in a single sheet of black glass. Something bell-shaped bulges under the glass at the far wall, and a cornerstone has fallen clear of the rubble, its carved date still legible.
em_choir_vestry.brief: A glassed-over vestry, a bell-shape under it.

variants.desc: A side room, roof half-collapsed, its robing-chest and shelves run together in a single sheet of black glass. Where the bell-shape stood, the glass lies broken open and empty now.

actions.label: climb into the fused frame (grace)
fx: You find the one gap the glass didn't quite seal and work the bell free through it, cracked along one side but whole enough to ring.
The glass gives no handhold worth trusting. It can be tried again.

actions.label: lever the fused frame apart (might)
fx: You brace and heave until the glass shears clean off the frame in one piece, the bell falling free of it, cracked but whole.
The glass holds. Your shoulder does not thank you for the trying. It can be tried again.

actions.label: read the fallen cornerstone
fx: A founding date, cut deep and sure — a decade earlier than the plaque's own. Somebody moved the chapel's birth forward in the telling, nearer an accident, further from a decision. You take a rubbing of it before you go.

actions.label: cross-reference the mason-mark
fx: The mason's mark matches one you've seen before, cut into the priory's own porch stone. Whoever built this chapel built the priory too, generations before either one burned — the same hands, hand in hand with the fire.

em_turned_cord.name: an ash-stiffened prayer cord
em_turned_cord.hint: someone climbed this far and went back down without it

em_true_date.name: a rubbing of the cornerstone's true date
em_true_date.hint: proof enough to refuse the Choir with, or to bargain its erasure away

em_chapel_bell.name: the chapel's recovered bell
em_chapel_bell.hint: cracked, but it might still ring where the singing is loudest

fx: You fit the Cinder Watch's warped clapper back into the bell's cracked mouth. It won't ring true again, but for the first time since the fire, it rings whole.

stages.text: The Choir sings quieter now, not rested — you struck its price off the stone, and the ridge took the trade.
The Choir has named its price: the true date, struck from record. Refuse it and endure, or pay it, in the chapel.
Something sings above Glasswick, in a chapel with no roof. Climb the ridge path and look it over.
Emberfall's grief waits somewhere west of Thornwold.

epilogue.text: The roofless chapel above Glasswick went quiet for good, once someone told it plainly there was nothing left to erase.
The Choir sings quieter above Glasswick, not gone. It paid its price in a mended bell nobody quite feels right ringing.
A fifth fire took the roofless chapel and changed nothing. Emberfall's Choir sings louder now than anyone there remembers it singing before.
The Choir of Ash was never answered. It sings above Glasswick still, and the glass-blowers still don't look up when it does.
Someone finally noticed Glasswick's plaque and its chapel's cornerstone disagree on a date. Nobody has fixed either one.
The Cinder Watch's lost clapper found its way home to the chapel bell, and the two ring true together now.
